parts.text: "Here is a research idea, the card a planner wrote for it, and a check of which existing research or industrial programmes would use its result, with the gaps that check found. Root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures? Idea: {\"title\":\"Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes\",\"text\":\"Exhaustive AlphaFold-Multimer, cryo-ET and MD modelling of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes across many variants, receptors and pH values would turn epitope geometry and pH-resolved kinetics from a per-complex experiment into a computed prior (method precedent: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518).\",\"root_link\":\"Bears on the \\"for which capsid–receptor binding signatures\\" half of the question — whether the epitope-geometry and pH-resolved-kinetics components of a signature can be computed instead of measured per complex.\",\"compute_open\":\"Model runs (capsid–receptor–glycan complexes predicted per pH condition): the largest amount a cited source reports is AlphaFold-Multimer runs of 5 structural models per capsid peptide with up to 20 recycles, paired with cryo-ET sub-tomogram averaging of 85,135 symmetry-expanded particles (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), and what is still unknown above that amount is whether any scale of computed coverage recovers epitope geometry and pH-resolved off-rates accurately enough to classify transcytosis versus retention, since the only quantitative pH-resolved benchmark in hand is a single measured pair (ALPL–VCAP-102, K_D ≈ 20 nM at pH 7.4 with rapid dissociation at pH 5.5: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9).\",\"sequential\":\"One run is a chain of roughly 10^9–10^12 integration steps at about 2 fs each, every step waiting on the previous coordinates, and a full answer needs several independent replicas per (capsid, receptor, pH) condition, with one replica keeping a GPU-resident MD engine busy for its whole length (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9281402/). The steps must run in order inside a single trajectory, but the answer can be assembled instead from many short independent trajectories started at the same time, which pays off when metastable states separate timescales so replicas decorrelate and weak scaling of independent runs beats strong scaling of one run (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9476681/); the nearest source that tried it is adaptive-sampling Markov state modelling, where wall-clock efficiency scaled linearly up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3637129/).\"} Card: **Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes · Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: unsure · PASS **Question.** Can computed capsid–receptor structures and pH-resolved MD contact lifetimes classify which AAV capsids cross brain endothelium versus stay inside cells? **What is known.** Adaptive-sampling Markov models matched one long villin run with up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration [s_bowman]; capsid work used 5 AlphaFold models per peptide [s_lrp6]. Whether computed pH-resolved contact lifetimes classify transcytosis versus retention at all; only one pair has measured pH kinetics [s_moyer]. **Hypothesis.** Epitope geometry from AlphaFold plus pH contact survival from many short replicas separates transcytosing LRP6/ALPL binders from retained capsids [s_lrp6][s_moyer]. **Restructuring.** One trajectory's 10^9–10^12 ordered 2-fs steps, each frame waiting on the last [s_jones]. Many short independent replicas run at once; contacts decorrelate inside each replica, so weak scaling beats one long run [s_kasson][s_kutzner_ens]. **If compute is the lever.** At 32 ten-ns replicas per condition the score reaches AUC ≥ 0.9 and pH ratio > 2, matching the 320-ns run [s_moyer]. **If not.** At 8–32 replicas the score stays at AUC ≤ 0.75 with no pH difference; the 320-ns run agrees, so more replicas do not help. **Test.** ColabFold AlphaFold-Multimer on 24 peptide–receptor complexes, then 32 ten-ns GROMACS replicas per pair at pH 7.4 and 5.5 on 8 V100s; compared with 320-ns sequential runs and published binding, domain and pH-release results [s_lrp6][s_moyer]. *Compute axis.* Independent 10-ns MD replicas per (peptide, receptor, pH) condition: 8–32 replicas, 3 levels. Closest prior: 5,000 [s_bowman], not beyond it. **Check first.** Reproduce the published AlphaFold-Multimer result: capsid peptides X1 and CAP-Mac bind LRP6 domain 1, not domains 3 and 4 [s_lrp6]. Tolerance: top-ranked of 5 models docks E1 not E3E4 for both peptides, at least 4 of 5 models agree. **Would not show.** Ten-ns contact-survival proxies, not millisecond off-rates. Peptide–domain fragments in water, not full glycosylated capsids. Six pairs, no cell-level transcytosis measured. *Cost.* Plans $945.84 of the $1,000 budget over 142 machine-hours, leaving $54.16. Main guess: MEM throughput on a two-V100 node, two independent runs [p], measured after $88.96 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 1.1× lower. 2 cost flags in the block. Card verdict: PASS 2/2 Programme check: [{\"name\":\"Voyager Therapeutics — TRACER capsid discovery platform / NeuroShuttle\",\"step\":\"Identification of the cell-surface receptor each BBB-penetrant TRACER capsid engages on brain vasculature, and whether that binding initiates receptor-mediated transcytosis, so capsids with a human-conserved receptor can be nominated as IV-delivered CNS gene therapy vectors (e.g. VY1706 tau-silencing program, ALPL-VYGR-NeuroShuttle).\",\"sum\":11},{\"name\":\"Dyno Therapeutics — AI capsid design with BBB-mechanism diversity\",\"step\":\"The BBB mechanism layer of AI capsid design: determining which blood-brain-barrier transport receptor an engineered capsid engages (human TfR1 for Dyno-yp2, ALPL for Dyno-9zh, or other Dyno-discovered receptors) and whether that engagement is conserved in human orthologues, before capsids are handed to CNS gene therapy partners.\",\"sum\":11},{\"name\":\"Gradinaru laboratory, California Institute of Technology — AAV capsid–receptor mapping program\",\"step\":\"Unbiased mapping of the human cell-surface and secreted proteins each engineered AAV binds (capsid–receptor interactome on brain endothelium-relevant receptors such as LRP6), plus structural and computational resolution of the capsid–receptor binding site, to explain which engineered capsids cross the BBB and by what binding signature.\",\"sum\":10}] Gaps found: [\"No programme has published a computed classifier of AAV capsid transcytosis versus endothelial retention validated against cell-level transcytosis; both Voyager and the Gradinaru lab decide this with Transwell assays, knockout mice or NHP in vivo screens, so the card's AUC is measured against its own labels and is uncalibrated to their decision endpoints.\",\"The card tests peptide–receptor-domain fragments in water and so does not cover the glycosylated capsid–receptor–glycan complexes its title claims: GPI-anchored ALPL, glycosylated LRP6 and CA-IV, and the full 60-mer capsid context are absent.\",\"Only one measured pH-kinetics pair exists (VCAP-102–ALPL, Voyager/Moyer 2025) to anchor the pH-ratio > 2 criterion; transferability of that release mechanism to LRP6-, TfR1- or CA-IV-binding capsids is untested.\",\"The compute axis (8–32 replicas of 10 ns per condition) is orders of magnitude below the screening scales these programmes operate at (~4E7-variant TRACER libraries, >6400-protein interactome screens, 10^4–10^7 pooled in vivo capsid designs at Dyno), so even a working score is not yet a screening tool.\",\"Ten-ns contact-survival proxies are not the millisecond-scale off-rates or endosomal release steps that determine transcytosis; if the pH ratio does not separate, the card's 'if not' outcome is likely, leaving all three programmes unchanged.\",\"Species context is unaddressed: the card uses human fragments only, while all three programmes select on orthologue binding and humanized or NHP models (LRP6 ~98% human/mouse identity, ALPL >92% across species, CA-IV only ~55% mouse/human).\"] Propose three close variants of the idea. Each changes one thing (the system studied, the quantity more compute buys, the comparison it is judged against, or the programme it is aimed at) so that its result would matter more to a named programme or close a named gap. Keep the rest of the idea. Name only systems, tools and programmes that appear above or that you are sure exist. Decide only from the text above; do not use tools.
